title: Dear Tommy, Love Me
genre: 1960s French yé-yé pop sung in English (Farfisa organ, jangling guitar, tambourine, girlish lead)
subject: a girl who ghostwrites her best friend's love notes to a boy, and the boy's replies keep describing details only she wrote, so she's the one falling for him
caption: 1960s yé-yé pop in the Paris teen-radio style, sung in English. Farfisa organ playing a bouncing staccato riff, clean jangling electric guitar strumming offbeat chords, a rounded bass guitar, light drums with a crisp backbeat, tambourine on every beat and handclaps in the bridge. Small-studio mono mix, bright and dry with light spring reverb. Female lead, bright and girlish with a playful lilt, two backing voices answering with ba-ba echoes, clearly sung. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 128 BPM, E major. Bouncy, giddy, comic mood. No synthesizer, no distorted guitar, no autotune, no hip-hop beat, no rap.
lyrics:
[Intro - organ, guitar and tambourine]

[Verse 1]
Dear Tommy, dear Tommy, I wrote it out neat
Janice can't spell and her handwriting's a mess
I put in the moon and the soda-shop door
Janice signs her name and I write him some more

[Pre-Chorus]
Then Tommy wrote back (oh, Tommy wrote back)
He mentioned my pencil, my pencil!

[Chorus]
Dear Tommy, love me, love me
You don't even know it's me
Janice signs the page, but I'm the girl
Who wrote you all that poetry

[Verse 2]
He says that he laughed at the line with the bus
I wrote it at lunchtime, not Janice, not us
He says that he blushed at the part by the gate
That's the one I wrote last, and it's late

[Pre-Chorus]
So Janice says, hey, write him more
Not knowing I'm done with the writing

[Chorus]
Dear Tommy, love me, love me
You don't even know it's me
Janice signs the page, but I'm the girl
Who wrote you all that poetry

[Bridge - handclaps and organ]
Tomorrow I'll sign it myself, myself
Tomorrow I'll sign it myself

[Chorus]
Dear Tommy, love me, love me
Now you're going to know it's me
No more Janice at the bottom of the page
Just my name, in my own pen

[Outro - organ, guitar and tambourine]
